mechanism_narrative: The sustained and accelerating increase in PARKS mobility, particularly the significant jump in the last week, indicates a growing public comfort with outdoor activities and leaving home, which will directly translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, or PARKS mobility sharply declines in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As people consistently spend less time at home (RESIDENTIAL decreases) and increasingly return to workplaces (WORKPLACES increases), their daily routines shift towards more out-of-home activities, leading to increased engagement with retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases for two consecutive weeks AND RESIDENTIAL decreases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains stagnant or decreases in the next two weeks despite continued shifts in residential and workplace mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The combined and consistent recovery in TRANSIT usage and WORKPLACES attendance signals a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting and work-related routines, which directly drives foot traffic to retail and recreation establishments over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks, even if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue their recovery trends.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (becoming less negative) indicates a relaxation of public health restrictions or a general increase in public comfort with essential outings, which typically precedes and enables a broader recovery in discretionary retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues to improve, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility, as observed in the last week, acts as a leading indicator for increased general outdoor activity and social interaction, which will translate to higher RETAIL_REC within the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week despite a large jump in PARKS mobility in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: The continuous decrease in time spent at residential locations signifies a fundamental shift in daily routines, pushing people out of their homes and into public spaces, which will eventually benefit retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility and decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests that people are increasingly comfortable and active outside their homes for essential activities, which will naturally extend to non-essential retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next two weeks, even with continued trends of less time at home and more essential outings.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility over the last two weeks, coupled with a steady increase in TRANSIT usage, indicates a return to a more structured work-week, which creates predictable demand for retail and recreation during lunch breaks and after-work hours, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show a positive trend for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Despite continued recovery in workplace and transit mobility, RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.
